A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on equivariant versus augmented training. All 21 pages of v2 and 27 pages of v3, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original training-dynamics experiments on synthetic graphs, synthetic shape segmentation and MNIST.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original CNN training-dynamics experiments, and Appendix E.2 retains empirical comparisons across four MNIST symmetry groups.

M1.justification: The analyzed model and training family expands from unrestricted MLP layers to affine spaces of admissible architectures with coefficient parameterizations and LL*/EE* gradient flows. Appendix A constructs convolutional, residual, attention, message-passing and recurrent architectures within this framework; these are substantive extensions beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The synthetic graph-connectivity and rotation-equivariant shape-segmentation tasks are removed. v3 evaluates MNIST classification only, retaining the four image symmetry groups from v2 Appendix E.2. The retained rotation-based MNIST experiment is distinct from the removed ROT segmentation experiment.

E2.justification: Nominal training, augmentation and manifest equivariance remain the comparison strategies, with unchanged membership in the corresponding four-group MNIST study. The added CNN experiment varies filter support and parameterization within augmented training as architectural controls.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 28-by-28 CNN protocol: 250 equivariant epochs followed by 10 augmented epochs, SGD with batch size 100, MSE loss, and learning rates 5e-4 then 2.5e-4. It measures drift by batch and epoch. This is an additional protocol; the retained 14-by-14 MNIST study still accumulates gradients over the full dataset.

E4.justification: The new CNN analysis directly tests compatibility through cross versus skew filter support, and parameterization through partially unitary versus non-unitary embeddings. It adds detailed initial-epoch drift trajectories. The earlier controlled four-group study connecting symmetry-space dimension to drift is retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 4 introduces median trajectories across 30 trials per condition, whereas v2's reported trajectories use means. Both show individual runs, and the retained appendix experiment preserves its 30-run mean reporting. There is no reported increase in repetitions for retained results or addition of confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 4 reports substantially less drift for the unitary cross-support CNN than for skew-support and non-unitary variants; Section 4.2 describes the former settling around 1e-3. Graph-classification and shape-segmentation results disappear. The four-group MNIST plot is identical in v2 Figure 6 and v3 Figure 7, so it supplies no new same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the compatibility condition, generalized stationary-point and stability theorems, parameterization-dependent invariance, and extensive architecture and compatibility derivations. Appendix C replaces abstract matrix counterexamples with an explicit network, loss and dataset construction. The feature-averaging formulation and several Fourier-projection propositions and proofs from v2 are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the claims from MLPs to constrained architectures and make relative geometry central. Equality of equivariant stationary points now explicitly requires commuting projections, while invariant augmented flow additionally requires unitary parameterization. The claim that augmented stability can fail despite equivariant stability remains.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving compatibility, parameterization, stochastic drift and numerical problems from ill-conditioned embeddings, while cautioning against generalizing the CNN drift ranking. It retains the symmetry-dimension heuristic but removes v2's suggested non-equivariance penalty and extended global-flow discussion. Future work now explicitly emphasizes stochastic training.

D1.justification: v3 adds CNN filter, channel, padding, pooling and normalization specifications, embedding initialization details, and hardware and computation information for 90 trials. Conversely, it omits v2's Fourier-projection implementation instructions and explicit learning rate and augmentation-pass procedure for the retained MNIST study. The code repository location remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to attention, SE(3)-transformers, Vector Neurons and Fulton and Harris, and tentatively positions its general equivariant-transformer formulation as novel in Appendix A. The existing augmentation and training-dynamics related-work argument is largely retained; the PyTorch reference is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, theoretical exposition and conclusion are substantially rewritten around compatibility and parameterization. Related work becomes an introduction subsection, and the appendices are reorganized around architecture constructions, compatibility, counterexamples, proofs and experiments. The author list also adds Oskar Nordenfors and changes order.

P2.justification: v3 adds framework and geometry displays, filter-support diagrams, CNN architecture and drift figures, and a pooling illustration. It removes graph- and segmentation-specific visuals, redraws the retained MNIST architecture, reorganizes dimension tables and adopts a different document layout. v2 Figure 6 is redisplayed unchanged as v3 Figure 7.

improvement.justification: The broader framework, explicit applicability conditions, model-level counterexample and targeted CNN controls offer substantive gains. However, unlike v2 Proposition 3, v3 Theorem 3.11(1) establishes Hessian positivity only on TL, then applies it to rotated directions not guaranteed to remain there; Appendix B explicitly permits such non-invariance. This unresolved proof gap, alongside narrower empirical coverage and omitted reproduction details, prevents a reliable judgment of net improvement.
